statement: The province should prioritize funding for public transit over highway expansion.

passages.title: The Tyee: The BC Conservative Platform - A Road Map to the 1950s
passages.quote: As for public transit, the Conservatives want to build out the SkyTrain to Newton in Surrey, put in regional rail service in the Fraser Valley and “implement a zero-tolerance policy for drug use, threats and violence on public transit.” Again, they say nothing about funding.

passages.title: CPBC Policy Declaration (March 2025)
passages.quote:
Public Transit and Passenger Rail
13.05 To build the public transit BC needs, the Conservative Party of BC will:
 (a) Extend SkyTrain to Newton in Surrey.

passages.quote: To build the public transit BC needs, the Conservative Party of BC will:

passages.title: CPBC Policy Declaration (March 2025)
passages.quote:
Reliable funding for reliable transit
13.07 The Conservative Party of BC will:
 (a) Fully fund TransLink for two years to maintain uninterrupted, reliable service.
 (b) Audit and reform TransLink's financial model to ensure the long-term availability of funding
 that not just maintains service, but fuels expansion for the future.

passages.title: The Tyee: The BC Conservative Platform - A Road Map to the 1950s
passages.quote: They aren’t everything the party could do, but it’s a start. Article 13 deals with transportation, which the Conservatives associate mostly with cars. They would build new bridges all over the province, including “a new Ironworkers Memorial Bridge with expanded capacity for both cars and public transit services.” And they would “replace the George Massey Tunnel as soon as possible.” How such projects would be funded is not mentioned.
